statement: Every student at a school chose exactly one lunch option, and the results are shown in a pie chart. The pizza sector has a central angle of $126^\circ$ and the salad sector has a central angle of $54^\circ$. Exactly $36$ more students chose pizza than chose salad. How many students are at the school?

choices.misconception: I worked out how many students chose salad, 72 degrees for 36 students means 54 degrees is 27 students, and I stopped there.
I worked out how many students chose pizza, 126 degrees is 36 x 126 / 72 = 63 students, and I stopped there.
I added the angles, 126 + 54 = 180 degrees, and matched that to the 36 students, so 360 degrees became 72.
I found 63 pizza students and 27 salad students and added them, forgetting the students who chose other options.

hints: The difference in the number of students matches the difference in the angles.
The pizza sector is $126^\circ - 54^\circ = 72^\circ$ larger than the salad sector, and that extra slice stands for $36$ students.
A $72^\circ$ slice is one fifth of the whole circle, so $36$ students are one fifth of the school.

solutions.reliable: In a pie chart the angle of a sector is proportional to the number of students it represents. The pizza sector is $126^\circ - 54^\circ = 72^\circ$ larger than the salad sector, so $72^\circ$ stands for $36$ students. The whole circle is $360^\circ = 5 \times 72^\circ$, so the school has $5 \times 36 = 180$ students. Check: pizza is $\frac{126}{360} \times 180 = 63$ students and salad is $\frac{54}{360} \times 180 = 27$, and $63 - 27 = 36$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
